title: I Gave an AI a Body — Cyrus Clarke, MIT Media Lab
talk_summary: An MIT Media Lab researcher connects an OpenClaw agent to a 900-pin shape display and lets it develop its own gesture vocabulary through a closed-loop generation/scoring/human-validation pipeline.

takeaways.technique: Generate-many, gate, score, human-verify loop for producing a validated artifact set
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent loops over a database of candidate gestures, passes them through validation gates for human legibility, an agent scores the outputs, and a human verifies the survivors before storing them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: go through some validation gates to try to make sure that the expressions are legible or readable for humans ... An agent then scores those as they come out ... at the end there's a human in the loop
takeaways.numbers: 32 good gestures after several weeks of looping

takeaways.technique: Precomputed response repertoire to cut latency
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of generating every response through the slow LLM path, the system selects from a pre-built repertoire of validated gestures so common responses are near-instant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we could design a body language and give the intelligence a repertoire of gestures ... it could probably respond much more quickly
takeaways.numbers: responses dropped from 45s-2min to near-instant for yes/no
